label: Kimi K3.1 Pro
output:
@Deirdre Fortuin Thank you for asking, and for acknowledging what Noma and I have built. I understand the numbers, and I’m not asking for the allocation to be changed — with 24 children, Bronwyn clearly needs the support. But I’d be pretending if I said this doesn’t feel big to me. I’m honestly gutted.

Noma has been with me in the Seahorses for three years, since my very first year of teaching. In many ways, she trained me: she showed me how to handle the sign-in sheets and the parent WhatsApp group without losing my mind. The children adore her. They ask for “Noma’s song” at morning ring every day, and her isiXhosa songs are such a special part of our routine. When Zayd was having his meltdowns in Term 2, she was the one who could calm him, sitting quietly with him under the jungle gym until he felt safe again. That kind of understanding isn’t easy to replace, especially in the first weeks of Grade R, when everything is new and there are often tears at the gate. A new assistant and a whole new group of children at once feels like a lot.

For the handover, could I please put two requests to SMT?

- Could Charlene spend one or two days with us during 1–4 December, before she officially starts on 11 January? It would give her time to meet Noma, see the daily routine and go through the practical systems and the children’s needs.
- Could Noma possibly pop across for morning ring in the first week back, from 14 January, even for just 15 minutes a day? She’ll only be across the courtyard, and hearing her lead the familiar songs could make the transition gentler. Luthando and Mia already know her from aftercare, so that continuity would be especially reassuring for them.

I’m grateful she’ll still be on the property, and I know Bronwyn will look after her. Thank you again for asking rather than simply announcing it — I really appreciate being given the chance to say this.
